author: sjm41
body:
* **InterPro ID / label**
Hexokinase, N-terminal (IPR022672)
Hexokinase, C-terminal (IPR022673)
* 
* **Example sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel Hexl (FBgn0042711)

* **Description of issue**
Hexl is annotated as a hexokinase pseudo enzyme, but is getting '[phosphotransferase activity, alcohol group as acceptor](https://flybase.org/reports/GO:0016773)' via IPR022672 and IPR022673 mappings.
Could you check if either of these domain entries map to the catalytic domain? If not, the GO:0016773 annotation should probably be removed.
title: InterPro2GO issue: Hexokinase, N-terminal (IPR022672) & Hexokinase, C-terminal (IPR022673)

author: tony787
body:
Dear Steven,
Different hexokinase isoforms differ in the location of their functional active site(s). 
If these two InterPro entries are matching a pseudo enzyme, I'm willing to remove the term from both.
Changes will be visible in the next InterPro release.
Best wishes,
Toni
